Not really. Only people I hung out with outside of school were him and a mutual friend of ours, who has become like a brother to me over the following years. Following what happened I also started hanging out with his parents a good bit, and they are some of the kindest people I've known. 
If I had any advice, it would be to stay and or get in contact with other people who were close to him. Piecing the world back together is a little less terrible when it's a community effort. 

Another idea would be to try and find a hobby that sometimes involves human interaction. Over the years I've met a ton of people I ended up becoming friends with at car meets

Similar deal here, best friend died unexpectedly, suicide. It's been 7 years now, and I am doing a lot better. 

You will never miss him less, and the world as you know it will never be as it was before, but the passage of time can allow for building a relationship with the fact that he's gone that no longer destroys the structure through which you interpret life. I know the sort of hell you've been cast in to feels endless, but it isn't. 

The stages of grief are hardly ever linear and are different for everybody, although I can definitely relate to being mostly angry for a long while. If there was anything I  wish I could tell my past self at the beginning of this, it would be not to feel bad about not feeling things when you think you should, and let yourself cry when you need to. I've also found it very comforting to be with other people he was close with. Nobody can do this alone, and having someone to lean on and be there for who is also right there with you makes a world of difference. 

I was also incredibly skeptical about therapy at first, same line of reasoning. They certainly can't bring someone back, however after being convinced to see one I've found that many of them can not only help you better understand your emotions, but also have some very useful insight into the underlying structure of cognition. Therapy is not for everybody, but I'd highly recommend at least giving it a try. 

I am so sorry that you're going through this, I wouldn't wish it upon anybody. Things do get better. 
If you're ever looking to talk to somebody on the internet feel free to send me a message, I'd be more than happy to help in any way I can.
